evidence: The docs/datasets/<code>_validation_ranges.yaml files are written by manage_dataset_documentation.py as per-dataset records. Each page links one as 'Download the YAML snapshot used for this validation' (for example gt21/index.html).

Those validations ran on legacy files, which the reference page says may use other signs, with the unflipped run band. Mirroring the snapshot makes the downloadable record differ from the ranges that produced the page's figures and pass rates.
AGENTS.md keeps historical artifacts explicitly legacy until reconverted, and acceptance item 3 says legacy files checked against old ranges remain labelled legacy.
The sign_rule_conversions note discloses the change, but the page still says the file is the snapshot used.
The 11 snapshots carry byte-identical entries: copies of the then default.
Centres: level -0.17..-0.01 (wide, near-symmetric bands, so the sign hardly matters); incline +0.07..+0.24; decline -0.32..-0.17; stair_ascent +0.19, +0.25; stair_descent +0.11, -0.11, -0.05.

Absolute level, the same argument as for run: incline and stair-ascent centres are positive, which under rule B would be posterior tilt from either documented zero. Uphill and stair climbing tilt the pelvis forward, so these read anterior-positive.
Cross-task order, which does not depend on the zero: incline and ascent are above level, and level is above decline. Rule B predicts the reverse, because forward tilt is more negative.
Decline, descent and level are individually ambiguous.

These snapshots were therefore coherent old-convention records, and the run-only edit made them internally mixed. If the snapshots were meant as rule-B guidance rather than records, all 17 walking/stair pelvis entries would need the same flip, and the page text would need to change. Reverting avoids both.

checks.area: pelvis analysis, run zero, missing options
checks.result: mostly right; run evidence understated; one cheaper option missing
evidence: Run band: the worker says it reads anterior-positive 'only if the zero is upright standing'. Under rule B, +0.3 rad is about 17 deg posterior tilt. That holds from the LocoHub zero (PSIS-ASIS forward horizontal; standing is then about -0.17 rad) and from a neutral-standing OpenSim pelvis_tilt zero. Running is anteriorly tilted. The band would be rule B only if its zero sat at least 0.3 rad anterior of posture; no documented zero in the repo does that. An OpenSim pelvis_tilt from a 180 deg heading also flips sign and gives the same anterior-positive reading. So the run band disagrees with rule B under every documented zero, unless its source was wrong in a way the files cannot show.

Can the zero be inferred from the ranges? Not reliably. The composition thigh - hip (centres) at run phase 0 gives -0.18 rad (ipsi) but +0.50 rad (contra), and sit/stand gives no correlation with the pelvis centres. Tuned band centres are not composable, so the range files cannot set the run zero. Older snapshots support the reading: the gt21 snapshot carries the same run band, and fr12 has incline centres positive and decline negative, which reads anterior-positive.

Transition: bands are nearly symmetric (centres -0.17 to +0.02, widths about 1.4 to 1.7 rad), so they work as magnitude checks. Flipping them changes almost nothing; they do not need to be withdrawn for sign reasons.

Missing option: keep the transfer and transition entries (they already read as rule B or are sign-insensitive) and withdraw only the 4 run entries per profile (or flip them, which is the bolder call given check 2). This is cheaper and more honest than withdrawing all 16. Flipping only the sit/stand entries would be wrong, because they already read as rule B.

Option C's handoff note says withdrawal needs a CORE-01 loader change. It does not: deleting a profile's pelvis entries makes the signal 'unchecked' (no applicable range), and an unchecked signal does not block eligibility in assess_observations. It is a scope change against acceptance item 1 ('only exact negation'), which is José's call anyway.
BASELINE_COMMIT 569ee8f4... is HEAD, and git diff of contributor_tools/validation_ranges is empty, so the pin matches the files.

Hiding risk: _baseline returns None for any git show failure, so a missing commit (shallow clone, rewritten history) skips every baseline test as 'not tracked at the baseline commit'. A missing commit should fail, or skip with a distinct reason. Confirmed by setting a nonexistent hash: _baseline returns None.

The pin compares phase bounds only, not top-level or task metadata (time_ranges, waveform_ranges, required_features, review_status). No range file currently has time_ranges or waveform_ranges, so nothing is hidden today; a future sign-bearing waveform_ranges entry would not be pinned.
strokepig_ranges.yaml is untracked, so it is skipped and unpinned (disclosed).

The 8 sign signatures are correct and each discriminates against an exact mirror. Independence across the two profiles is partial: 3 of the 8 rows (knee swing, run foot, braking GRF) are byte-identical in default and gtech_2024, so the parametrization over both files adds no evidence for those rows.

The loader claims hold. impaired_ranges.yaml fails with "must contain a 'tasks' mapping", and validation_ranges_with_adduction.yaml fails on non-finite incline_walking moment bounds. Range files are unchanged from HEAD, so both failures predate CORE-07.
